[serious][quietly] A widow was walking behind her only son's body, carried out on a bier to be buried. He was all she had left.

[matter-of-fact] The law was simple: touch a dead man, and you were unclean. Everyone kept their distance. That was survival, not cruelty.

[reflective][deliberate] Jesus walked toward her instead of away. And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, <speaker name="jesus">"Weep not."</speaker>

[awe][slow] Then he touched what no one else would touch: and he came and touched the bier, and they that bare him stood still.

[deliberate][emphasized] Under that same law, the touch should have made him unclean. It didn't work that way with him. And he said, <speaker name="jesus">"Young man, I say unto thee, Arise."</speaker>

[awe] And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.

[awe][reflective] Death didn't spread from the boy to Jesus. Life spread from Jesus to the boy.

[reflective][deliberate] That is still the only direction he touches anything dead in you. Not to catch what's wrong with you — to give you what's his instead. He touched a funeral, and it became a homecoming.
